## `GET /v1/hooks/types`

- `data`
- `data.dimension`
- `data.platform`: Platform slice ('all' when not filtered).
- `data.category`: Category slice ('all' when not filtered).
- `data.snapshot_date`: Date of the daily snapshot the stats come from.
- `data.types`
- `data.types[].value`: Taxonomy value. Includes 'none' (no discernible hook) for corpus accounting.
- `data.types[].video_count`: Hooks in the corpus with this value for the selected slice.
- `data.types[].share_of_corpus`: Share of the slice corpus (0-1).
- `data.types[].total_views`
- `data.types[].avg_views`
- `data.types[].median_views`
- `data.types[].avg_weighted_score`: Mean Virality Score. Reads negative for most types because about half of all videos get fewer views than their creator has followers; do not rank typ…
- `data.types[].median_weighted_score`: Median Virality Score: the typical outcome for a video using this hook type.
- `data.types[].p90_weighted_score`: 90th-percentile Virality Score: how good the winners get.
- `data.types[].strong_hit_rate`: Share of videos using this hook type that scored strong or better (Virality Score >= 18), 0-1. The best single number for "which hook types work".

## `GET /v1/hooks/search`

- `data`
- `data[].hook_text`: Verbatim opening line — a contiguous substring of the first ~6 seconds of speech, or the frame-1 on-screen text when there is no spoken hook. Never p…

- `data[].visual_hook_type`: First-frame visual classification (12-value vocabulary). Orthogonal to hook_type. Null for slideshows.
- `data[].content_type`

- `data[].language`: Detected ISO language code of the content.
- `data[].brand_safety_tier`: Brand-safety tier of the source content (safe | low_risk | medium_risk — higher-risk content is excluded from the corpus).
- `data[].outlier_ratio`: How far the video's views outran its author's follower count. The raw outlier signal.

- `data[].usage_count`: How many corpus posts open with this exact hook (case- and whitespace-insensitive). Identical hooks are collapsed to their strongest source, so this…
- `data[].video`: The source post this hook was extracted from (the strongest one when several posts share the hook).

- `data[].video.author_handle`: Creator handle on the platform.
- `data[].video.author_followers`: Creator follower count at last sync.

- `data[].match_type`: How the hook matched q. exact: the hook IS the query (reverse lookup hit). contains: the hook contains the phrase; this tier is ranked by Virality Sc…
- `data[].match_score`: Trigram similarity between the query and hook_text (0-1); 1 for exact matches. Informational: ordering is by match_type first. Null when no q was giv…
- `pagination`: total and total_pages are null: the number of matches is not computed (it is not small). has_next_page is exact. Results stop at the top 1,000; page…
- `pagination.page`
- `pagination.limit`
- `pagination.total`: Always null: the total number of matches is not computed for this ranked read. It is unknown, not zero and not small. Page with has_next_page.
- `pagination.total_pages`: Always null, for the same reason as total.
- `pagination.has_next_page`: Exact: true when at least one more result exists after this page.
- `pagination.has_prev_page`

## `GET /v1/topic-trends/today`

- `data[].trends[].exemplar_count`: Example videos the topic shows after the check against the topic, one per creator (not capped by top_exemplars).
- `data[].trends[].top_exemplars`: Example videos that passed the check against the topic, one per creator, most-viewed first (checked before unchecked). Capped per request by the `top…

- `data[].trends[].top_exemplars[].url`

- `data[].trends[].top_exemplars[].is_paid`: True when the post is paid distribution rather than organic reach: TikTok marked it boosted (ad spend) or a Paid partnership / Promotional content, I…
- `data[].trends[].detected_at`: When this trend was first detected and entered its day container.
- `data[].trends[].last_seen_at`: Last intra-day analysis run that re-confirmed this trend. Null when the trend was only seen once.
- `data[].trends[].origin_region_codes`: Provenance for cross-regional (e.g. 'global') trends: the regions whose independent detections evidenced this trend. Null for plain regional trends.
- `data[].trends[].global_confidence`: Confidence (0-1) that this is genuinely the same cross-regional trend. Only set on synthesis-promoted global trends.
- `data[].trends[].velocity_today_count`: Videos matching this trend in the last 24h at discovery time.
- `data[].trends[].velocity_median_views`: Median exemplar views at discovery time.
- `data[].trends[].momentum`: Live momentum signal, refreshed every ~2h by a stats-only loop. Null until the first snapshot runs for this trend, or while the topic has fewer than…
- `data[].trends[].momentum.score`: Normalized 0-1 heat derived from the current views/hour of the trend’s exemplars. Higher = hotter right now.
- `data[].trends[].momentum.status`: Lifecycle status. `new` = just detected, `rising` = accelerating, `steady` = flat, `fading` = decelerating.
- `data[].trends[].momentum.views_per_hour`: Hourly view growth of the example videos between the last two snapshots, counting only videos measured at both.
- `data[].trends[].momentum.updated_at`: When momentum was last recomputed (snapshot loop, ~2h cadence).

- `data[].trends[].trend.id`
- `data[].trends[].trend.name`
- `data[].trends[].trend.description`
- `data[].trends[].trend.category`: What the topic is about. Null for a topic not categorised yet (usually minutes old). Values may be added over time; treat an unknown value as "other".

## `GET /v1/raw/meta/ads/search`

- `data`: One Ad Library page (about 30 ads on the first page, about 10 after). Can be empty (still billed).
- `data[].id`: Ad Library ID.
- `data[].url`: The ad in the public Ad Library.
- `data[].advertiser`
- `data[].advertiser.page_id`: Facebook page ID of the advertiser.
- `data[].advertiser.name`
- `data[].advertiser.avatar_url`: Page avatar URL on the Facebook CDN. These links expire.
- `data[].advertiser.url`: The advertiser's Facebook page.
- `data[].is_active`: True while the ad is running.
- `data[].started_at`: First day the ad ran, ISO 8601 UTC.
- `data[].ended_at`: Last day the ad ran, ISO 8601 UTC. Null while the ad is active.
- `data[].publisher_platforms`: Where the ad runs, lowercase: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads.
- `data[].media_type`: `video` when any creative has a video, else `image` when any has an image, else `none` (text only).
- `data[].creatives`: The ad's creatives. A carousel or catalog ad has one per card. Can be empty. Image and video links are Facebook CDN URLs. They expire after a few day…
- `data[].creatives[].body`: Primary text of the ad.
- `data[].creatives[].title`: Headline.
- `data[].creatives[].description`: Link description under the headline (on catalog ads often a price).
- `data[].creatives[].caption`: Display domain or caption under the media.
- `data[].creatives[].cta_text`: Button text.
- `data[].creatives[].cta_type`: Button type, lowercase.
- `data[].creatives[].link_url`: Where the ad links to.
- `data[].creatives[].image_urls`: Image URLs. Image and video links are Facebook CDN URLs. They expire after a few days; download what you need to keep.
- `data[].creatives[].videos`
- `data[].creatives[].videos[].hd_url`: HD video URL. Image and video links are Facebook CDN URLs. They expire after a few days; download what you need to keep.
- `data[].creatives[].videos[].sd_url`: SD video URL. Image and video links are Facebook CDN URLs. They expire after a few days; download what you need to keep.
- `data[].creatives[].videos[].preview_image_url`: Poster image URL. Image and video links are Facebook CDN URLs. They expire after a few days; download what you need to keep.
- `data[].variant_count`: Ads the Ad Library groups under this one because they use the same creative. Null when not grouped.
- `data[].page_categories`: Categories of the advertiser's page.
- `data[].reach`: People reached. Only for ads shown in the EU or UK (exact, lower = upper) and political or issue ads (a range). Otherwise null.
- `data[].reach.lower`: Lower bound. Null when open.
- `data[].reach.upper`: Upper bound. Null when open (e.g. ">1M").
- `data[].spend`: Amount spent, as a range. Political and issue ads only; otherwise null.
- `data[].spend.lower`: Lower bound. Null when open.
- `data[].spend.upper`: Upper bound. Null when open (e.g. ">1M").
- `data[].spend.currency`: ISO 4217 currency of the bounds.
- `data[].impressions`: Impressions, as a range. Political and issue ads only; otherwise null.
- `data[].impressions.lower`: Lower bound. Null when open.
- `data[].impressions.upper`: Upper bound. Null when open (e.g. ">1M").
- `data[].platform_data`: Ad Library fields outside the shared schema, snake_case. A key is absent when the ad has no value. Keys: `display_format` (e.g. `image`, `video`, `dco`, `dpa`, `carousel`), `collation_id`, `ad_categories` (e.g. `political`), `paid_for_by` (political disclaimer), `page_like_count`, `contains_digitally_created_media`, `targeted_countries`, and for ads shown in the EU or UK `audience` ({ gender, age_min, age_max, locations }), `payer`, `beneficiary`.
- `pagination`
- `pagination.next_cursor`: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. Null on the last page.
- `pagination.has_more`: True when next_cursor is set.

Keys: `page_alias`, `entity_type`, `verification` (e.g. `blue_verified`), `instagram_verified`, `country`, and on advertiser ads `ad_count` (ads that match the filters, as the Ad Library counts them; it stops at 50,001).
- `pagination`
- `pagination.next_cursor`: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. Null on the last page.
- `pagination.has_more`: True when next_cursor is set.

## `GET /v1/satellite/creator/status/{job_id}`

- `data`: Job state — shape varies by status field (processing | completed | failed)
- `data.status`
- `data.finalized`: Always false while the main lookup is still processing. Included for shape uniformity with the completed variant.
- `data.pending_jobs`: Always an empty array while the main lookup is processing.
- `data.pending_jobs[].type`: Stable identifier for the kind of secondary job. Use this to switch on the field where the result will appear (see `result_path`).
- `data.pending_jobs[].status`: Current non-terminal state of the job. Once the job reaches a terminal state (ready / failed / skipped) the entry is removed from `pending_jobs[]`.
- `data.pending_jobs[].job_id`: Optional opaque identifier for the underlying job, when one exists. Useful with `poll_url` to fetch the result directly.
- `data.pending_jobs[].poll_url`: Path (relative to api.virlo.ai) you can GET to fetch the result of this job once it is ready. Free to call.
- `data.pending_jobs[].result_path`: Dot-path inside the parent resource's response body where the completed result will appear. Useful for clients that re-fetch the resource instead of…
- `data.pending_jobs[].webhook_event`: Name of an event from the existing `SUPPORTED_EVENTS` list that fires when this job reaches a terminal state. Subscribe to it via POST /v1/webhooks t…
- `data.pending_jobs[].started_at`: When the job entered its current state (ISO 8601 UTC).
- `data.pending_jobs[].retry_after_seconds`: Suggested minimum delay (seconds) before polling again. Respect this to avoid hitting rate limits.

- `data.result.comparison.top_videos[].is_this_video`
- `data.result.comparison.key_findings`: Plain sentences on how this video differs, written only when the numbers clear a bar. Differences, not proven causes.
- `data.result.comparison.key_findings[].kind`
- `data.result.comparison.key_findings[].text`
- `data.finalized`: Always true once the analysis completed: nothing else runs after it. Same done signal as the other async status replies.
- `data.status`
- `data.error`
- `data.finalized`: Always true when the analysis failed: no further work will happen.
